issues.description: Method getTotalNumberOfStudents: the problem statement's UML (problem_statement.md) declares the method signature as getTotalNumberOfStudents(): String (UML line shows a String return type), while the reference solution (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) implements the method with signature public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() (returns an int). The textual task in the problem statement (line 41) instructs students to check the UML for the expected return type, so this mismatch will confuse students about whether to implement/return a String or an int and may cause tests or grading to expect a different type than the solution uses.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Recommended: update the UML in problem_statement.md (and any related text) to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int to reflect that the method returns a numeric total, and ensure tests and examples expect an int. Alternatively, if the intent is to return a String, change the reference solution and tests to return a String (e.g., String.valueOf(total)) and update the example to match. Prefer the int return type for semantic clarity (a count is numeric).
